_comment: DE4SDV INC-DRIVING-001 slice 10b, DRAFT, bench-only, not yet validated.
The DE4SDV stack configuration of the SDV Core VM for the driving
operational state. It replaces the reference stack's
/vendor/etc/someip/vsomeip_config.json, as the AEBS frame bench's does.
It offers no SOME/IP service: the SDV Core VM consumes the three events
that someipd on the S-CORE host offers (service 0x4df0, instance 0x0001,
eventgroup 0x0001, events 0x8001/0x8002/0x8003, reliable TCP 30510, ICD
section 3). Each event's payload is the ICD section 3 SOME/IP struct (no
length field, big-endian); the broker translates it in REFLECTION mode into
the typed message de4sdv.driving.v1.DrivingOperationalState.
__SCORE_SOMEIP_PEER__ is the S-CORE host's address on the VXLAN segment;
scripts/stage_sdv_core_interop.sh renders it from SCORE_SOMEIP_PEER.
The service is marked secure and accepted only from that address (the
AEBS frame bench's setting): with service discovery enabled, vsomeip
3.1.37.1 processes an offer for a known service from any sender unless
the service is secure, so an SD offer from the IVI VM could otherwise
redirect the subscription. AOSP's vsomeip copy may carry patches, so the
runbook verifies the effect; the residual goes to GAP-MW-012 as in the
AEBS bench. The SD group stays 224.0.0.0 (GAP-MW-047).
The earlier increment's frame service 0x4dee (reliable 30509, provider
192.168.98.1) stays configured exactly as the tree carries it
(some_ip/vsomeip_stack/vsomeip_config.json): this file replaces that one, so
dropping it would silently unconfigure the proven service. The stage script
merges the two acceptances into one entry when both providers have one address.
